gauges.label: VIX (expected S&P volatility)
gauges.meaning: How much turbulence options traders are paying to protect against.

gauges.label: VIX vs 3-month VIX
gauges.meaning: Above 1.0 means traders fear the next month more than the next three: acute stress.

gauges.label: S&P 500 below its all-time high
gauges.meaning: How far the index has fallen from its peak.

gauges.label: S&P 500 vs its 200-day average
gauges.meaning: Below zero is the classic line for a downtrend.

gauges.label: Nasdaq 100 below its high
gauges.meaning: The tech-heavy index that leads most risk-on and risk-off swings.

gauges.label: Bitcoin below its high
gauges.meaning: A gauge of speculative risk appetite.

gauges.label: Corporate credit spread (Baa minus 10-yr)
gauges.meaning: Extra yield lenders demand from companies. Rising fast is credit stress, which separates corrections from crises.

gauges.label: Yield curve (10-yr minus 2-yr)
gauges.meaning: Negative (inverted) has preceded most US recessions.

gauges.label: 10-year Treasury yield
gauges.meaning: The cost of money for the whole economy.

sources: Yahoo Finance ^GSPC since 1950, ^VIX since 1990, ^VIX3M since 2006, ^NDX since 1985, BTC-USD since 2014
meta.method: Percentile = share of past days with a lower reading. Forward returns are S&P 500 price changes after past days whose reading fell within ±5 percentile points of today's. Episodes start after a gap of more than 21 trading days.
